newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed,S&P 500s higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed,S&P 500s higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed, as profit-taking in technology stocks weighed on most contracts and trimmed gains in the most-active Standard & Poor's 500s, traders and analysts said.
"We would have ended the day in much better condition had it not been for the beating in tech stocks," one S&P 500 floor analyst said.
Nasdaq 100 futures ended pit trade down more than 11.00 points, as the Nasdaq composite index lost 13.41 points or 1.0 percent due to the selloff in technology stocks.
"Intel got creamed today," another trader said.
March S&Ps clung on to gains in thin trade after an extremely volatile day. March set its 10.80-point range in less than an hour and a half of trading this morning.
Several traders were relieved that March S&Ps managed to close with any gains at all after settling Thursday's equally choppy session near the daily low at 734.00.
"After yesterday's performance, we are happy S&Ps and the Dow (industrials) closed with any gains at all," one trader said.
However, March S&Ps finished the week 11.25 points lower from last Friday's close.

One floor analyst said fair value for March would be at 6.90 points on Monday. Arbitrage buy programs are seen at an 8.40 point premium and arbitrage sell programs are seen at a premium of 6.60 points.
March Nikkei futures closed higher after trading in narrow ranges.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 1.90 at 736.40, Value Lines were up 3.75 at 678.75, New Composites were up 1.65 at 388.05, Nikkeis were up 145 at 20,505, Midcap 400s were off 0.80 at 252.05, and Nasdaq 100s were down 11.75 points at 842.50.
